review_notes: I read the whole file and the related files: DiagonalCartan.lean (`coe_typeDDiagonalCartanBasis_apply`), Weight.lean (`diagonalBivector_def`, `spinAction_diagonalBivector_basis`), and the uses of these lemmas in the other TypeD files and TypeB/RootGenerators.lean. I found no rewrite cycles. The `typeDBasis_inl` and `typeDBasis_inr` lemmas look fine. I did not run Lean, so the claims about which simp lemmas fire first rest on reading the lemma statements. The two findings below are the only simp-interface problems I found.

findings.problem: This is the one `@[simp]` lemma that actually fires on `typeDQuadraticEquiv` applied to a diagonal Cartan generator. The reason is that `coe_typeDDiagonalCartanBasis_apply` is `@[simp]` and first rewrites `↑(typeDDiagonalCartanBasis i)` to `⟨typeDDiagonalMatrix (Pi.single i 1), _⟩`. After that rewrite, only this lemma matches. It is `private`, so the simp rule is part of the interface but cannot be named or cited from other files. The public companion `typeDQuadraticEquiv_typeDDiagonalCartanBasis` states the same fact in the `typeDDiagonalCartanBasis` form. Because of the earlier rewrite, that form is not the simp-normal form, so it is not tagged `@[simp]` and `simp` never uses it. TypeB/RootGenerators.lean cites the private name in its docstring, which suggests it is meant to be a reusable interface.
findings.proposed_change: Make `typeDQuadraticEquiv_typeDDiagonalMatrix_single` public (drop `private`) and keep `@[simp]` on it. Add a docstring saying it is the simp-normal form after `coe_typeDDiagonalCartanBasis_apply`. Keep `typeDQuadraticEquiv_typeDDiagonalCartanBasis` as a non-simp rewrite lemma for `rw`, and say in its docstring that simp reaches the same result through the matrix form.
findings.benefit: The lemma becomes visible in the API and in docs, and other files (including the TypeB proofs that mimic it) can cite it by name in `simp only [...]` or `rw`. It also makes clear which of the two statements is the canonical simp rule.

findings.problem: The `@[simp]` lemma's right-hand side is `↑(typeDDiagonalCartanBasis i)`. The `@[simp]` lemma `coe_typeDDiagonalCartanBasis_apply` rewrites that to the matrix subtype `⟨typeDDiagonalMatrix (Pi.single i 1), _⟩`. So the lemma as stated is not in simp-normal form, and `simp` will finish at a different expression from the stated RHS. It also does not match the forward simp lemma, whose normal form is the matrix subtype. Two of the equivalence's simp lemmas therefore end at different forms of the same generator: the forward direction ends at the matrix form, and the `symm` direction is stated in the Cartan-basis form but rewritten to the matrix form.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma with the matrix-form right-hand side, `⟨typeDDiagonalMatrix (Pi.single i 1), typeDDiagonalMatrix_mem_typeD _⟩`, so that it is the simp-normal inverse of `typeDQuadraticEquiv_typeDDiagonalMatrix_single`. If the Cartan-basis form is wanted, keep it as a separate non-simp lemma. The existing proof can be reused: it can be restated using `coe_typeDDiagonalCartanBasis_apply` or `symm_apply_apply`.
findings.benefit: Simp then produces the same expression as the lemma states, and the two directions of the comparison use the same canonical form. This avoids a rule whose output is rewritten again, and it avoids a silent difference between the stated and the actual simp results.
